question.problem: What is the center of the hyperbola $4{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}-16y+4x=0?$
question.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}-16y+4x & =0 \\ 4{y}^{2}-16y-{x}^{2}+4x & =0 \\ 4[{y}^{2}-4y]-[{x}^{2}-4x] & =0 \\ 4[(y-2)^{2}-4]-[(x-2)^{2}-4] & =0 \\ 4(y-2)^{2}-16-(x-2)^{2}+4 & =0 \\ 4(y-2)^{2}-(x-2)^{2} & =16-4 \\ 4(y-2)^{2}-(x-2)^{2} & =12 \\ \frac{(y-2)^{2}}{3}-\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{12} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center is $(2,2).$
